key_insight: ReuF2F tests coding agents on 244 formalized open undergraduate research problems, with the best-performing model resolving only about 40%.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark provides a containerized Lean 4 setting for evaluating agents on research problems with machine-checkable proofs.
method: Formalize open REU problems across diverse mathematical subfields in Lean 4.
Place each problem and its logical negation in a Lean project within a Docker container.
Use Leanimum-agent, built on mini-SWE-agent, as a unified evaluation harness.
evidence_signal: Across 244 problems, the reported best-model resolution rate of approximately 40% indicates substantial remaining difficulty.
watch_item: Less prominent problems may reduce solution exposure, but their suitability for held-out evaluation still depends on monitoring public solutions and possible training contamination.
paper_title: ReuF2F: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Formalized Undergraduate Research Problems
